comparator.name: Spanish Language and Culture (Spaanse Taal en Cultuur; current programme title: Spaanse en Latijns-Amerikaanse studies)
comparator.sourceNotes: The selected Spanish and Latin American Studies abroad pathway closes 60+60+60. It keeps the required 30-EC Spanish/Latin American university semester separate from 30 EC of genuine free profiling, and counts the 12-EC Spanish-language thesis once. Abroad entry requires at least 54 first-year EC plus attendance in year-two semester one; part-time exchange starts no earlier than year three. An unweighted home alternative is not stacked. Diagnostic test and recurring tutoring are mandatory zero-credit formation. Current course evidence supports Dutch, Spanish and English instruction.

alternatives.label: Colonial histories, global literature & cultural memory
alternatives.concept: Study literature, empire, colonial and postcolonial histories, migration, cultural memory, heritage, media and language/power across transatlantic and global contexts. Treat these as related humanities and social-science approaches while preserving the absence of Spanish-language proficiency and a sustained Spain/Latin America sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The label names the completed curriculum’s literature, empire, migration, media, heritage and cultural-memory content without claiming Spanish-language study or a full Spain/Latin America curriculum.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and ten level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; the only formal prerequisite, Introduction to Brain & Behavior for Psycholinguistics, occurs two semesters earlier. Introductory literary, historical, sociological and film study precedes advanced interpretation, media, heritage and research. No Spanish-language prerequisite or proficiency is invented.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & language in cultural expression
alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic and media forms create meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal cultural production. Preserve Spanish proficiency and Spanish-specific linguistics as explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film and media; it is labelled as cultural-expression study and not as Spanish proficiency or Spanish linguistics.
progression: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and eight level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Introductory literature, rhetoric, sociology and film/media precede advanced stylistic, persuasive, creative, interpretive and documentary work. No Spanish-language competence is implied by this progression.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Native American Histories, European Union Politics and three art/heritage courses are replaced by Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action, Persuasive Communication, Creative Communication Laboratory and From T.V. to TikTok. The change shifts advanced study from colonial histories, heritage and cultural memory to language, rhetoric and mediated expression.

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. A third Spanish-proficiency, translation and source-language programme is not feasible because the workbook contains no Spanish acquisition sequence, advanced Spanish grammar, sociolinguistics, translation or Spanish-language academic writing. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as Spanish proficiency.

Both address contemporary societies, social movements and civil-society change; UCR includes Latin American cases but is not a dedicated Latin America course.

The required 30-EC Spanish/Latin American university semester has no scheduled UCR equivalent.
The genuine 30-EC profiling space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study global literature, colonial and postcolonial histories, migration, cultural memory, heritage, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and language/power. UCR does not offer Spanish proficiency progression, Spanish grammar and sociolinguistics, translation, Spanish-language academic writing, or a cumulative Spain and Latin America literature/culture sequence, so these are related humanities routes rather than Spanish Language and Culture equivalents.
